title: Analytic Derived Six Operations And Duality

items.title: Proper continuous maps of topological spaces
items.statement: Let $X$ and $Y$ be topological spaces ([[def-topological-space]]) and let $f:X\to Y$ be continuous ([[def-continuous-map-top]]). Then $f$ is **proper** when for every compact subset $K\subseteq Y$ ([[def-compact-space]]) its preimage $f^{-1}(K)$ is a compact subset of $X$. Compactness of subsets is the intrinsic condition of [[def-compact-space]], namely compactness of the subspace $f^{-1}(K)$ with the subspace topology ([[def-subspace-topology-top]]); by [[lem-compactness-of-a-subspace-is-ambient]] it is equivalent to the ambient reading, so a subset is compact exactly when every cover by open subsets of the ambient space has a finite subcover, and the two readings are used interchangeably below without further comment. This is the notion of properness used throughout the analytic six-operation development on this page, where the spaces involved are locally compact Hausdorff ([[def-locally-compact-space]], [[def-hausdorff-space]]). The stability properties consumed by the later items — closed inclusions are proper, composites of proper maps are proper, properness is preserved by base change along a continuous map into a Hausdorff space, and fibres and closed subspaces of a proper map inherit properness — are proved in the lemma `lem-proper-continuous-map-stability` on this page. The definition involves no choice principle: it quantifies over compact subsets and preimages only.

items.title: Basic stability of proper continuous maps
items.statement: Let $X$, $Y$ and $Z$ be topological spaces ([[def-topological-space]]), with properness as in [[def-proper-continuous-map]]. 1. If $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ is the inclusion of a closed subset, then $i$ is proper. 2. If $f:X\to Y$ and $g:Y\to Z$ are proper continuous maps, then the composite $gf:X\to Z$ is proper. 3. If $f:X\to Y$ is proper, $Y$ is Hausdorff ([[def-hausdorff-space]]) and $u:Y'\to Y$ is continuous, then the pullback $$f':X\times_YY'\longrightarrow Y',\qquad X\times_YY'=\{(x,y')\in X\times Y': f(x)=u(y')\},$$ the subset carrying the subspace topology of the product ([[def-product-topology]], [[def-subspace-topology-top]]), is proper. 4. If $f:X\to Y$ is proper, then every fibre $f^{-1}(y)$ is a compact subset of $X$. 5. If $f:X\to Y$ is proper and $S\subseteq X$ is closed, then the restriction $f|_S:S\to Y$ is proper. 6. If $f:X\to Y$ is proper and $Y$ is locally compact Hausdorff ([[def-locally-compact-space]]), then $f$ is a closed map: the image of every closed subset of $X$ is closed in $Y$. These are the stability properties consumed by the closed-support functor $f_!$ on this page; no choice principle is used in any of them.

items.title: Derived operations on analytic field sheaves
items.statement:
Let $k$ be a field and let $X,Y$ be locally compact Hausdorff spaces
([[def-locally-compact-space]], [[def-hausdorff-space]]). Write
$\operatorname{Sh}_k(X)$ for the category of sheaves of $k$-vector spaces
([[def-sheaf-on-topological-space]], [[def-sheaf-cohomology-derived-global-sections]])
viewed as modules over the constant ring sheaf $k_X$, and form derived
categories in those sheaves ([[def-derived-category-of-an-abelian-category]]).
For a continuous map $f:X\to Y$, set $f^*=f^{-1}$
([[def-inverse-image-presheaf-and-sheaf]]) and define $f_!F$ on an open
$V\subseteq Y$ to consist of the sections of $F$ on $f^{-1}(V)$ whose closed
support ([[def-support-of-a-sheaf-section]],
[[def-compactly-supported-global-sections]]) maps properly to $V$, properness
being that of [[def-proper-continuous-map]] together with its stability lemma
[[lem-proper-continuous-map-stability]]. Under AC ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]),
$Rf_*$ and $Rf_!$ are computed on bounded-below $k$-linear injective
replacements. Tensor means the signed total tensor over $k$
([[def-sheaf-tensor-product]]) and internal derived Hom is the injective
construction of
[[lem-bounded-analytic-field-sheaves-have-derived-tensor-hom-and-pullback-pushforward-adjunctions]]
([[def-sheaf-hom]]).

Suppose the uniform all-fibre-open cohomological dimension bound of
[[lem-finite-fibre-dimension-gives-bounded-fibrewise-soft-resolutions]] holds,
and choose its finite resolution $k_X\to K$; for an open $U\subseteq X$ put
$K_U=j_{U!}j_U^*K$ ([[def-extension-by-zero-abelian-sheaf]],
[[def-c-soft-sheaf]]). For a bounded-below injective complex $I$ on $Y$,
define the exceptional inverse-image candidate to be the sheaf complex with
open sections $\operatorname{Hom}_Y^\bullet(f_!K_U,I)$.
[[thm-compactly-supported-derived-pushforward-has-exceptional-inverse-image-adjoint]]
proves that this candidate is a sheaf complex and is independent of the chosen
resolution. Set $\omega_X=a_X^!k$ and $D_XA=R\mathcal Hom(A,\omega_X)$ when the
terminal map satisfies the same finite-dimensional hypotheses. Constructible
restriction is a separate geometric theorem; none of these definitions asserts
a generic six-functor axiom.

The prescriptions are those of Verdier's exposé: $f^*$ is the exact inverse
image, $f_!$ is the sheaf of sections whose closed support is proper over the
base — a presheaf by the local nature of properness, whose sheaf property for every sheaf is proved by the exceptional-adjoint theorem
recorded in `justified_by` — $Rf_*$ is derived from the direct image
[[def-direct-image-sheaf]] on bounded-below injective replacements, and the
terms of the chosen finite resolution are fibrewise $c$-soft, not
necessarily $c$-soft on $X$. Their acyclicity for $f_!$ follows from the
fibre formula in its well-definedness theorem; the restricted fibre sheaves
are compact-support acyclic by
[[lem-c-soft-field-sheaves-are-compact-support-acyclic]].
The ordinary-operations lemma also supplies the flasque acyclicity
([[def-flasque-sheaf]]) used to compare resolutions. AC supplies the injective replacements and finite fibrewise-soft
resolution; the proper-support sections, extension by zero and the
exceptional candidate itself are choice-free constructions. Cohomological
shifts obey $H^i(A[r])=H^{i+r}(A)$ in the convention of
[[def-derived-category-of-an-abelian-category]].
items.strategy: This item is definitional: it fixes the categorical setting, the functors, and the exceptional candidate, and its only well-definedness obligation is the exceptional-inverse-image adjoint theorem of the next item on this page (recorded as that definition's justified_by target at authoring, not as a prerequisite of this definition). Source route: Verdier, expose 300, SS1-SS2 pp. 339-343 (definition and left exactness of $f_!$, the finite fibrewise-$c$-soft resolution $k_X\to K$, and the construction of $f^!$ from $\operatorname{Hom}^\bullet_Y(f_!K_U,I)$), and Stacks Project, Cohomology of Sheaves SS12 (flasque acyclicity, used by the resolution). Step 1 fixes $\operatorname{Sh}_k(X)$ as an abelian category of module sheaves over $k_X$ and its derived category. Step 2 defines $f^*=f^{-1}$, $f_!$ by proper support of sections, $Rf_*$ and $Rf_!$ by bounded-below injective replacements, and recalls $\otimes_k^L$ and $R\mathcal Hom$ from the ordinary-operations lemma. Step 3 assumes the uniform all-fibre-open bound, fixes the finite resolution $k_X\to K$ of the bounded-fibrewise-soft-resolution lemma, and forms $K_U=j_{U!}j_U^*K$ for opens $U$. Step 4 defines the exceptional inverse-image candidate by the section complexes $\operatorname{Hom}^\bullet_Y(f_!K_U,I)$; the adjoint theorem proves this is a sheaf and independent of the choices, so the definition is well posed. Step 5 defines $\omega_X=a_X^!k$ and $D_X=R\mathcal Hom(-,\omega_X)$ under the same finite-dimensional hypotheses. No generic six-functor axiom, no constructible restriction and no unrestricted right adjunction is asserted here.

items.axiom_use: AC is declared because the definition of $Rf_*$ and $Rf_!$ through bounded-below injective replacements consumes the enough-injectives embedding for module sheaves over the constant ring sheaf (inside [[lem-bounded-analytic-field-sheaves-have-derived-tensor-hom-and-pullback-pushforward-adjunctions]]). The proper-support sections, extension by zero and the exceptional candidate itself are choice-free constructions.

items.title: Exceptional inverse image as the adjoint of derived proper-support image
items.statement: Assume AC ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) and the uniform all-fibre-open dimension bound $d$ of [[lem-finite-fibre-dimension-gives-bounded-fibrewise-soft-resolutions]]. For a continuous map $f:X\to Y$ of locally compact Hausdorff spaces, the proper-support functor $f_!$ of [[def-derived-operations-on-analytic-sheaves-over-locally-compact-spaces]] is left exact, satisfies $(Rf_!A)_y\simeq R\Gamma_c(X_y,A|_{X_y})$ on every fibre, and maps bounded derived categories into bounded derived categories. Its exceptional inverse-image candidate $f^!$ represents the natural Hom transposition $$\operatorname{Hom}(Rf_!A,B)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}(A,f^!B)$$ for bounded source objects $A$ and bounded-below target objects $B$, and has lower cohomological bound $\inf(B)-d$. When the later geometric theorem proves that $f^!$ preserves the bounded constructible subcategory, this becomes the right adjunction $Rf_!\dashv f^!$ there; on that bounded constructible specialization the adjunction unit, counit and resolution comparisons satisfy the triangle, identity and cocycle laws. The proper-support evaluation constructs the counit directly. The proof constructs this adjoint from a finite fibrewise-soft resolution and generator complexes, independently of Verdier biduality; it does not infer an unrestricted $D^+$-source adjunction from the bounded-source generator argument.
items.strategy: Direct construction under AC and the uniform all-fibre-open dimension bound d. Proper-support sections glue by finite relatively compact covers. Fibre restriction is injective because a proper support has closed image, and surjective by the compact collar argument. Restricted injectives are c-soft, so the fibre formula supplies f!-acyclicity and dimension at most d. The finite fibrewise-soft resolution k_X→K and exact extension-by-zero Čech resolution give the candidate H_K(I), whose terms are flasque and vanish below inf(I)−d; Čech cycles are acyclic by backwards dimension shifting. Open generators E_U=j_U!k_U identify derived sections with Hom(f!K_U,I). Construct the field-linear cover G(E)=⊕_(U,s)E_U and descending recursion on the cone-kernel equations, obtaining a quasi-isomorphism M→A. Use the valid zigzag A←M→K⊗M. Direct sums have finite-coordinate compact-support stalks; K⊗M has f!-acyclic terms. Finite cohomological dimension and low canonical truncation compare this model with Rf!A. The bounded-diagonal Hom comparison against an injective replacement of H_K(I) then proves the derived Hom transposition. For a closed proper support Q, set K_Q=i_Q*i_Q*K; the exact open/closed quotient gives supported Hom sections, and precompose with k_V→f*k_Q→f*K_Q to construct the counit. Taking H0 gives the natural bounded-source transposition and lower bound. Once geometric outputs are bounded constructible, this becomes a full adjunction, with triangle and cocycle laws by uniqueness. No unrestricted D+ source adjunction is inferred. Source: Verdier, exposé 300, §§1–3, pp.339–345.

items.axiom_use: AC is assumed and consumed through the enough-injectives embedding inside the ordinary-operations lemma (via [[lem-bounded-analytic-field-sheaves-have-derived-tensor-hom-and-pullback-pushforward-adjunctions]]), through [[lem-c-soft-field-sheaves-are-compact-support-acyclic]] and through the choice-dependent bounded-above flat resolution [[lem-abelian-sheaves-admit-bounded-above-flat-resolutions]] used to construct the generator complex. The support and stalk arguments are otherwise choice-free.

items.title: Support localization, base change, projection and trace calculus
items.statement: Under the preceding locally compact and finite-dimensional hypotheses, $u^*Rf_!\simeq Rf'_!v^*$ for Cartesian squares; proper maps have $Rf_!=Rf_*$, giving proper ordinary base change. Bounded tensor factors satisfy the projection formula. Proper-support direct images compose canonically. On the bounded constructible specialization proved by the subsequent local duality construction, exceptional adjoints also compose canonically; their units, counits and traces respect composition and Cartesian pasting. For a closed inclusion $i:Z\to X$ with complement $j$, $i^!$ is the derived functor of $i^{-1}\Gamma_Z$, and both localization triangles hold. Locally, $R\mathcal Hom(i_*k_Z,A)$ is $R\Gamma_ZA$. This lemma does not assume or claim extraordinary dual base change before constructible biduality.
items.strategy: Assume AC. Sources: Verdier, expose 300, SS1.2 p. 340 (base change), SS1.5 p. 341 (compose), SS2.3 p. 342-343 (the trace $\gamma:\ f_!f^!(G)\to G$) and SS2 p. 341-342 (flasque terms); Stacks Project, Cohomology of Sheaves SS17-SS18 (base change map and proper base change, as an independent verification of the canonical exchange) and SS21 (the localization triangle of $R\Gamma_Z$). Step 1 (closed support). Put $\Gamma_ZF=\ker(F\to j_*j^*F)$; it has zero stalks off $Z$, hence equals $i_*i^{-1}\Gamma_ZF$ by [[lem-sheaf-supported-on-a-closed-subset-is-a-pushforward]], and $i^!_0=i^{-1}\Gamma_Z$ is right adjoint to the exact $i_*$ and preserves injectives; the stalk exact sequence from [[lem-extension-by-zero-short-exact-sequence]] gives both localization triangles, and tensor-Hom transposition with the closed adjunction identifies $R\mathcal Hom(i_*k_Z,A)$ with $R\Gamma_ZA$ locally on every open. Step 2 (base change). For a Cartesian square, inverse image of an injective on $X$ restricts on each fibre of $f'$ to the restriction of the original injective, hence is fibrewise-$c$-soft and $f'_!$-acyclic; the fibre-stalk formula of the exceptional-adjunction theorem identifies $u^*f_!I\to f'_!v^*I$ on stalks, and applying to an injective complex proves $u^*Rf_!\simeq Rf'_!v^*$; for proper $f$ this is ordinary proper base change. Step 3 (projection). On fibres, $f^*B$ is the constant complex $B_y$ and tensoring a $c$-soft complex with a vector space stays $c$-soft, with $\Gamma_c(E\otimes V)=\Gamma_c(E)\otimes V$ for finite tensor presentations; this proves the canonical map $Rf_!A\otimes B\to Rf_!(A\otimes f^*B)$ is a stalk isomorphism and identifies it with the adjoint of the counit tensored with $\mathrm{id}$. Step 4 (composition and traces). The support definition proves $(gf)_!=g_!f_!$ (proper support over $Y$ and $Z$ agree by the two properness conditions), and applying the two support functors to an injective resolution gives the canonical composition isomorphism; the trace homomorphisms are the actual counits of the exceptional adjunction, and $\mathrm{tr}_{gf}=\mathrm{tr}_g\circ Rg_!(\mathrm{tr}_f)g^!$ follows by transposing the identity of $f^!g^!$. Step 5 (pasting). The two composites of base-change maps in a pasted square restrict a representative section to the same fibre section before deriving, and both projection composites send a pure tensor to the same pullback tensor; all identities hold in the dg resolution model. Extraordinary proper exchange $u^!Rf_*\simeq Rf'_*v^!$ is deliberately NOT claimed here: it is proved only after constructible biduality on this page, in the later duality theorem that is not a prerequisite of this lemma.

items.title: Constructible Verdier duality and complex orientation
items.statement: Assume AC and the actual finite conical/triangulation and derived-incidence-model suppliers listed below. On the analytic space $X$ of a separated finite-type complex algebraic variety, constructible complexes admit the fixed-space finite models required by those suppliers. Then $\omega_X=a_X^!k$ and $D_X=R\mathcal Hom(-,\omega_X)$ preserve bounded constructible objects and the natural evaluation $A\to D_XD_XA$ is an isomorphism. On a smooth complex $d$-variety, the complex orientation normalizes $\omega_X\simeq k_X[2d]$. For constructible maps for which the geometric supplier proves the stated bounded outputs, $Rf_*D_X\simeq D_YRf_!$, $D_YRf_*\simeq Rf_!D_X$, and $f^!\simeq D_Xf^*D_Y$. Proper base change has the coherent extraordinary dual exchange $u^!Rf_*\simeq Rf'_*v^!$. The fixed-space triangulation is not an assumed globally simplicial model of $f$.
items.strategy: Direct under AC and the actual finite conical/incidence suppliers. F6 cites the arbitrary-sheaf polyhedral dimension theorem independently of constructible finite cochains. The finite affine-open extension-by-zero resolution has degree -p, so compact-support terms bounded by d yield total degrees at most d on every open of X. Closed-pushforward compact-support transport gives the same bound on all opens of every fibre, licensing a_X and f exceptional adjoints. Terminal adjunction and tensor–Hom yield RΓ(U,D_XA)=RHom_k(RΓ_c(U,A),k) and dualizing transitivity; these are global derived Hom complexes. Oriented balls give ω_X=or_X[n], hence k_X[2d] for smooth complex d-folds. On each affine open choose the supplied finite deleted-boundary model and finite diagram injective resolution. For each relatively closed cell C_σ, define its interior extension E_σ=i_σ*a_σ!k. Compact-support half-line contractions and oriented sectors compute D_X I_σ=E_σ[dim σ] and D_X(E_σ[dim σ])=I_σ. Controlled complex-stratum ball×normal-cone models first establish bounded algebraic constructibility of ω_X; internal-Hom constructibility then applies to A and ω_X. Evaluation is an isomorphism on cogenerators and propagates through the finite resolution cones; affine restriction proves global biduality. Internally localized exceptional adjunction gives Rf*D_X=D_YRf!, and biduality gives its reverse exchange and f!=D_Xf*D_Y. This proves bounded constructibility of f! and the genuine constructible adjunction. Dualize canonical ordinary proper base change for the coherent extraordinary exchange. Source: Verdier §§1–3 and the local suppliers listed in deps.

The local cellular dual computations and the orientation normalization are choice-free. AC is also inherited through F6's arbitrary-sheaf Cech comparison and open/closed compact-support transport; finite cover selection and finite simplex contraction use only finite choice.

items.title: Coherent six operations on analytic constructible field sheaves
items.statement: Assume AC and the actual geometric and derived-incidence suppliers of the Verdier theorem. For analytic algebraic maps on its proved constructible subcategory, the six operations $f^*,Rf_*,Rf_!,f^!,\otimes_k^L,R\mathcal Hom$ have their three adjunctions, composition and identity comparisons, ordinary proper and extraordinary proper base change, projection formula, support localization, dualizing transitivity and trace. The comparisons commute with Cartesian pasting, composition of maps, evaluation and trace, giving a coherent pull-push product calculus. For a locally trivial product projection with finite-type smooth fibre $F$, the actual finite product cochain model gives $R\mathrm{pr}_*\mathrm{pr}^*B\simeq B\otimes_k C^*(F;k)$, with its ordinary unit. Smooth base change for $Rf_*$ holds whenever a supplied factorization $f=p\circ j$ has $p$ proper and $j$ an open inclusion with the conical local models below; proper maps already satisfy it. Their finite constructible models commute with extension of coefficient fields. Geometric output preservation is the exact geometric supplier, not an additional axiom.
items.strategy: Direct application of the proved ordinary, support/trace and Verdier suppliers on actual bounded constructible objects. Their canonical units, counits, evaluation and section comparisons give the adjunction, projection, localization, identity, composition and proper exchange laws. Product projections use finite incidence resolutions on quasi-projective charts; for a general separated finite-type fibre, finite affine-open Čech descent assembles the same finite fibre complex and its ordinary unit k→C*(F;k). Smooth open-inclusion base change follows on contractible ball product charts; combine it with proper base change only for a supplied open-proper factorization. Scalar extension commutes with finite cochains and finite-dimensional duals; use f!=D_Xf*D_Y for the exceptional comparison. No infinite injective product comparison or general compactification theorem is asserted.

references.title: J. Bernstein, V. Lunts, Equivariant Sheaves and Functors, Part I §§1.4–1.8 (six operations, Verdier duality, smooth maps and smooth base change)
A. A. Beilinson, J. Bernstein, P. Deligne, Faisceaux pervers, Astérisque 100 (1982); §1.4 recollement t-structures and §2.1 perverse sheaves on stratified spaces

items.axiom_use: AC is assumed and consumed through the geometric suppliers [[lem-complex-algebraic-stratifications-have-finite-conical-cochain-models]], [[lem-finite-simplicial-constructible-sheaves-have-a-derived-incidence-model]] and [[lem-locally-contractible-metric-spaces-have-singular-constant-sheaf-cohomology]], and through the injective/incidence models of the support-and-trace and Verdier suppliers. The finite product-projection and coefficient-extension computations are otherwise choice-free.

items.title: Actual analytic constructible sheaves admit coherent six operations
items.statement: Assume AC ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) and let $k$ be an arbitrary field. On separated finite-type complex varieties, the ordinary analytic sheaf operations restrict to bounded algebraically constructible complexes $D_c^b(-;k)$ ([[def-algebraically-constructible-complex-of-analytic-field-sheaves]]): $f^*\dashv Rf_*$, $Rf_!\dashv f^!$, the tensor/internal-Hom adjunction, coherent composition, support localization, ordinary and extraordinary proper base change, the projection formula and trace. Proper $f$ satisfies $Rf_!=Rf_*$. Verdier duality is involutive there and exchanges these adjoints. On a smooth complex $d$-fold $\omega_X=k_X[2d]$, and for a smooth map of relative dimension $d$, $f^!=f^*[2d]$. Coefficient extensions commute with these operations on bounded constructible inputs. The bounded constructibility and finite coefficient models are those of [[lem-complex-algebraic-stratifications-have-finite-conical-cochain-models]] and [[lem-finite-simplicial-constructible-sheaves-have-a-derived-incidence-model]].
items.strategy: Assume AC. Sources: Bernstein-Lunts, Part I SS1.4.1-SS1.4.6 (tensor-Hom, composition, adjunctions, proper equality, open localization triangles and base change) and SS1.6-SS1.7 (dualizing object, Verdier duality for continuous maps, and smooth maps of relative dimension $d$), together with the finite resolution construction of Part I SS1.9/Appendices A and the derived-category simplicial comparison; BBD, Faisceaux pervers, SS1.4.1-1.4.10 (the recollement localization triangles giving localization and gluing), as an independent treatment. Step 1: the actual compact-support adjoint and coherent six-operation suppliers construct the functors and their adjunction units/counits, not just unrelated isomorphisms; their ordinary coherent composition, Cartesian exchange, projection/trace and localization diagrams are the asserted diagrams, including proper equality $Rf_!=Rf_*$ and the smooth local-product comparisons. All vector-space and injective constructions apply over an arbitrary field; their signed cochains use only $0$ and the units $\pm1$, so no characteristic hypothesis enters. Step 2: the actual finite conical and incidence suppliers prove bounded constructibility and finite coefficient models for the stated finite collection, so the constructed operations restrict to $D_c^b$ and their finite local cochain comparisons commute with field extension; the actual support construction for compactly supported operations is used, and no infinite tensor of injective products is formed. Step 3: the oriented stratified Verdier supplier gives its evaluation isomorphism and identifies the dualizing object on a smooth complex $d$-fold with $k[2d]$ through the positive complex orientation; its adjunction construction gives duality exchange and the stated smooth extraordinary pullback $f^!=f^*[2d]$, and all these maps use the same ordinary units/counits and orientation, so their coherence is the coherence of the actual construction. The integral orientation generator maps to the nonzero unit $1\in k$ over every field, including characteristic two.

references.title: J. Bernstein, V. Lunts, Equivariant Sheaves and Functors, Part I §§1.4–1.8 (six operations, Verdier duality, smooth maps and smooth base change) and §1.9 with Appendices A (acyclic maps)

items.axiom_use: AC is assumed and consumed through the geometric suppliers [[lem-complex-algebraic-stratifications-have-finite-conical-cochain-models]] and [[lem-finite-simplicial-constructible-sheaves-have-a-derived-incidence-model]] and through the injective/cochain models of the three analytic theorems. Every remaining step is a finite-dimensional or canonical comparison and is choice-free.

items.title: Ordinary middle perverse t structure, recollement and intersection complexes
items.statement: Assume AC ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) and let $k$ be any field. On $D_c^b(X;k)$ for a separated finite-type complex variety $X$, middle perversity is given on smooth complex strata $S$ by the two inequalities $H^q(i_S^*A)=0$ for $q>-\dim_{\mathbb C}S$ and $H^q(i_S^!A)=0$ for $q<-\dim_{\mathbb C}S$. These inequalities define a bounded t structure ([[def-canonical-t-structure-on-a-derived-category]]) on $D_c^b(X;k)$, independent of compatible refinement and gluing across algebraic open/closed decompositions. Verdier duality exchanges its two aisles. The heart is abelian and of finite length, and its simple objects are the intersection complexes $j_{!*}L[\dim_{\mathbb C}Z]$ of simple finite-rank local systems $L$ ([[def-locally-constant-sheaf-of-finite-rank]]) on dense smooth opens of irreducible supports $Z$. Open restriction is perverse exact. Heart objects have no negative Hom, and the endomorphism ring of a simple object is a division $k$-algebra. This is the ORDINARY category: no equivariant category, no normalization, no semisimplicity and no noncharacteristic theorem is used or asserted.
items.strategy: Direct recollement construction under AC, over any field. The localization adjunctions give the glued aisles; two truncation cones and the octahedron establish the truncation triangle. Finite strata give boundedness. Refining S to a codimension-c smooth T changes locally constant extraordinary restriction by [−2c], which proves compatibility and refinement independence. The finite-dimensional dual formula H^j(D_SK)=(H^(−j−2e)K)^∨ exchanges the middle aisles. For a heart map, the cone truncations and octahedron give kernel, cokernel and equal image/coimage. Define intermediate extension as the image of J!M→J*M for heart input M; on an e-dimensional smooth open use M=L[e]. Adjunction proves the no-boundary subobject/quotient characterization. Finite local transport and homotopy subdivisions show that subsystems are invariant stalk subspaces. Codimension-two ray avoidance moves loops into any dense algebraic open, preserving simplicity of a simple local system after restriction; strict boundary degree bounds show L[e] has no boundary subquotients. Simple objects are thus the intersection complexes on irreducible closed supports. For finite length, induct on support dimension and use a finite local-system series, right exactness of J!, and its boundary-supported kernels. Orthogonality proves negative Hom vanishing; a nonzero endomorphism of a simple object is invertible. Sources: BBD 1.4.10, 1.4.22–26, 2.1.13–16; §4.3 provides the étale analogue, while the analytic transport argument is proved locally in the carrier.

items.title: Shifted smooth complex pullback is exact for the middle perverse t structure
items.statement: Assume AC ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) and let $a:X\to Y$ be a smooth algebraic map of pure relative complex dimension $d$ between separated finite-type complex varieties, over an arbitrary coefficient field $k$. Then $a^*[d]$ is exact for the ordinary middle-perverse t structures of [[thm-ordinary-middle-perverse-t-structure-glues-and-has-simple-intersection-complexes]] on $D_c^b(-;k)$, and it commutes with their truncation and cohomology functors. Complex orientation gives $a^!=a^*[2d]$. If $a$ is surjective, its normalized pullback is conservative and reflects the perverse support and cosupport inequalities. The compatible finite stratifications used are those of [[thm-complex-algebraic-varieties-and-maps-admit-compatible-finite-stratifications]].
items.strategy: Direct support-and-duality proof under inherited AC. For each compatible target stratum S of dimension e, take components of the full inverse image a−1(S), smooth of dimension e+d; arbitrary source refinements need not have that dimension. Smooth product charts give a finite compatible pullback stratification. The identity H^q(i_T*a*A[d])=a_T*H^(q+d)(i_S*A) preserves the upper bound q>−(e+d). The proved six-operation supplier gives a!=a*[2d], so D_X(a*A[d])=a*D_YA[d]; self-duality of middle perversity proves lower preservation. Uniqueness of truncation yields commuting perverse truncation and cohomology. If a is surjective, stalkwise pullback reflects vanishings, and the same support and dual-support calculation reflects both inequalities and gives conservativity. This works over every field.

title: Analytic Derived Six Operations And Duality Examples

items.title: Dualizing and support shifts on the complex line
items.statement: With the conventions of [[thm-verdier-duality-on-oriented-stratified-complex-varieties]] and coefficient field $k$: on the complex line $\mathbb C$ (an oriented smooth complex 1-fold) the dualizing object is $\omega_{\mathbb C}=k_{\mathbb C}[2]$. For the closed inclusion $i:\{0\}\hookrightarrow\mathbb C$ one has $i^!k_{\mathbb C}=k[-2]$ and $i^!\omega_{\mathbb C}=k$. The example consumes the AC-assumed Verdier supplier; the displayed computation itself is choice-free.
items.strategy: Use the AC-assumed duality and support suppliers; the displayed calculation is finite and choice-free. For an oriented open disk U with closed compactification D, (D,∂D) computes compact supports and has one generator in degree 2, giving ω_C=k_C[2]. Localization at 0 identifies i!k_C with the relative cohomology of (U,U∖{0}); radial retraction of the puncture to S1 gives k[−2]. Thus i!ω_C=i!(k_C[2])=k[−2][2]=k. The route D_pt i* D_C gives the same signs. Sources: Verdier duality and the proved local support calculus.
